assignment: Online/adaptive decisions: OCO/regret, bandits/contextual bandits, MDP/Bellman, RL exploration/sample complexity, policy gradient/actor-critic, offline/model-based/deep RL limits, partial observation, imitation, safe/constrained decisions and adaptive inference.
extraction: PDF text extracted to complete page-marked plain-text files with PyMuPDF. PDF pages, not publisher pagination, are the primary exact range. Printed pages are also supplied where legible. Formulas and glyphs in the 1996 Brown report extraction are damaged; the cached PDF was used to check material formulas. No source text is reproduced in the dossier.

sources.title: Introduction to Online Convex Optimization, second edition
sources.author: Elad Hazan
sources.source_note: Author-posted open preprint; used after the publisher-hosted second-edition endpoint returned 403.

read_units.unit: Chapter 1: online protocol, regret, Hedge/weighted majority
Chapter 2: convex optimization, gradients, projections
Chapter 3: online gradient descent, strongly convex losses, lower-bound discussion
Chapter 5: regularized FTL, Bregman divergence, OMD, adaptive regularization
Chapter 6: bandit convex optimization, EXP3, FKM, SCRiBLe
Chapter 10: dynamic and adaptive regret, Fixed Share, FLH/FLH2

sources.proofs_hypotheses_gaps: The OGD upper-regret proof is displayed under bounded decision-set diameter and bounded subgradients. Hedge requires bounded losses and the specified comparator/feedback model. The lower-bound proof in Chapter 3 is partly an exercise. Projection existence and a Chapter 5 AdaGrad optimizer calculation are exercises; parts of Chapter 10 FLH analysis are deferred to exercises. The dossier does not treat these exercise statements as completed proofs.

sources.title: Bandit Algorithms
sources.author: Tor Lattimore and Csaba Szepesvári
sources.source_note: Author-hosted complete book PDF; content follows the Cambridge University Press edition with corrections and different page numbering.

read_units.unit: Chapter 4: stochastic bandit model, policy kernels, regret decomposition
Chapter 5: concentration inequalities and sub-Gaussian tools
Chapter 6: explore-then-commit
Chapter 7: UCB
Chapter 11: adversarial bandits and Exp3
Chapter 18: adversarial contextual bandits and Exp4
Chapter 19: stochastic linear/contextual bandits and LinUCB
Chapter 20: self-normalized, time-uniform linear confidence sets

sources.proofs_hypotheses_gaps: The stochastic UCB analysis assumes finite arms and independent 1-sub-Gaussian reward tables, with fixed-prefix union bounds to avoid concentration at a random pull count. Chapter 11 gives expected Exp3 regret and warns about high variance; high-probability Exp3-IX is an exercise. Chapter 18 gives expected Exp4 guarantees for finite actions and experts. Some Chapter 5 foundational inequalities are exercises. The Chapter 20 mixture-supermartingale argument supplies a time-uniform linear-regression ellipsoid under conditional sub-Gaussian noise, predictable designs, a positive ridge parameter, and a parameter-norm bound; these conditions must be preserved.

sources.title: Reinforcement Learning: An Introduction, second edition, complete draft
sources.author: Richard S. Sutton and Andrew G. Barto
sources.source_note: Author-posted complete draft; some figures were still being remade. HTTPS on the direct endpoint failed during acquisition, so the author's HTTP PDF was used.

read_units.unit: Chapter 3: finite MDPs, returns, Bellman equations
Chapter 4: dynamic programming and policy improvement
Chapter 5: Monte Carlo prediction, control, and off-policy sampling
Chapter 6: TD, Sarsa, Q-learning
Chapter 8: planning, Dyna, RTDP, search
Chapter 9: value function approximation and its limitations
Chapter 10: control with function approximation and average reward
Chapter 11: off-policy learning with approximation, deadly triad, counterexamples
Chapter 13: policy gradients, REINFORCE, baselines, actor-critic

sources.proofs_hypotheses_gaps: The policy-gradient theorem proof, policy-improvement proof, and several algorithm derivations are displayed. General value-iteration convergence and standard linear TD/Q convergence are stated/sketched with external citations rather than fully proved. Exploring-starts Monte Carlo control convergence is explicitly left open in the text. Continuing average reward assumes an ergodic steady-state distribution. Baird's counterexample and the two-state divergence calculation are explicit examples, not universal deep-RL theorems. Nonlinear approximation and actor-critic convergence are not established.

sources.title: Offline Reinforcement Learning: Tutorial, Review, and Perspectives on Open Problems
sources.author: Sergey Levine, Aviral Kumar, George Tucker, and Justin Fu
sources.source_note: Full 43-page review/tutorial; claims about later developments are limited to this 2020 review and its cited results.

read_units.unit: Complete manuscript: formulation, IS/OPE, dynamic programming, offline policy constraints/conservative values, model-based offline RL, applications, discussion, and references

sources.proofs_hypotheses_gaps: This is a review, not a single theorem paper. It states and discusses behavioral-cloning horizon dependence, importance sampling/doubly robust estimators, offline support and distribution shift, and model exploitation. Many formal guarantees are attributed to cited papers rather than proved here. No theorem is inferred from an empirical benchmark. The review's conclusions are time-bounded to its 2020 literature cutoff.

sources.title: Planning and Acting in Partially Observable Stochastic Domains
sources.author: Leslie Pack Kaelbling, Michael L. Littman, and Anthony R. Cassandra
sources.source_note: Readable full-text Brown technical report was used instead of a later scanned journal PDF whose text extraction was empty on many pages.

read_units.unit: Complete report; PDF page 2 blank; references on pp. 27-29

sources.proofs_hypotheses_gaps: Known finite transition and observation model; finite state/action/observation sets. Belief update and belief-MDP construction are derived. Finite-horizon policy-tree values are linear in belief, so their finite maximum is piecewise-linear convex. Witness/pruning complexity depends on the number of policy trees and can be exponential. The PDF text layer drops many formula symbols; formulas were checked in the cached PDF, and no formula was reconstructed from OCR alone. Model acquisition is explicitly outside the paper's scope.

sources.title: A Reduction of Imitation Learning and Structured Prediction to No-Regret Online Learning
sources.author: Stéphane Ross, Geoffrey J. Gordon, and J. Andrew Bagnell
sources.publication: AISTATS 2011, JMLR Workshop and Conference Proceedings 15, 627-635

read_units.unit: Complete article, all results, experiments, discussion, and references

sources.proofs_hypotheses_gaps: The reduction assumes strongly convex bounded surrogate losses for the stated no-regret rate, expert labels on learner-induced states through interaction, and a surrogate-loss/task-cost relationship with the stated coefficient u. The finite-sample statements use trajectory sampling and Azuma. The experiments are empirical, not theorem evidence. It is not a fixed-data/offline guarantee.

sources.title: Constrained Policy Optimization
sources.author: Joshua Achiam, David Held, Aviv Tamar, and Pieter Abbeel
sources.publication: ICML 2017, Proceedings of Machine Learning Research 70

read_units.unit: Complete main paper including CMDP setup, policy bounds, CPO derivation, approximation, experiments, discussion, references

sources.proofs_hypotheses_gaps: The main performance-difference bound's proof is referred to supplemental material and is not present in these ten pages. The idealized trust-region update and its bound are distinct from sampled linearized CPO with conjugate-gradient solves and line search. The paper's near-constraint claim is approximate expected discounted cost satisfaction, not a pathwise/hard safety guarantee. Experiments use simulated tasks.

sources.title: Time-uniform, nonparametric, nonasymptotic confidence sequences
sources.author: Steven R. Howard, Aaditya Ramdas, Jon McAuliffe, and Jasjeet Sekhon

read_units.unit: Complete article, main results, scalar proofs, applications, appendices, tables, and references

sources.proofs_hypotheses_gaps: The mixture theorem requires product measurability and a nonnegative supermartingale family; crossing control follows by Ville. The stitching proof and empirical-Bernstein self-normalization proof are included. Coverage is simultaneous over all times and stopping rules under the declared filtration/conditional assumptions. Matrix bounds rely on cited matrix-supermartingale facts from Howard et al. (2020), not reproved in this article; these are excluded unless separately sourced and proved. This Category 4 source/pair must not become a Category 3 prerequisite.

sources.title: Reinforcement Learning in Finite MDPs: PAC Analysis
sources.author: Alexander L. Strehl, Lihong Li, and Michael L. Littman

read_units.unit: Complete article, R-MAX/Delayed Q algorithms, main upper/lower proofs, appendices, and references

sources.proofs_hypotheses_gaps: Theorem 10 is a general escape-event reduction; Theorems 11 and 16 analyze R-MAX and Delayed Q-learning with an admissible heuristic. The finite discounted MDP has bounded nonnegative rewards, finite S/A, known discount, and explicit confidence/sample parameters. The online transition/reward samples are adaptively selected; the paper notes that martingale concentration is needed and refers its detailed proof elsewhere. The lower-bound theorem has deterministic-policy and one-state-at-a-time policy-change restrictions. PAC sample complexity counts non-near-optimal policy steps, not an output-only guarantee.

sources.title: Near-optimal Regret Bounds for Reinforcement Learning
sources.author: Thomas Jaksch, Ronald Ortner, and Peter Auer

read_units.unit: Complete article, UCRL2 and extended value iteration, main upper/lower proofs, appendices, and references

sources.proofs_hypotheses_gaps: UCRL2 assumes a finite communicating MDP with finite diameter, bounded [0,1] rewards, and average-reward benchmark; the learner knows S/A but not the model. Theorem 2 proves the high-probability regret bound; Theorem 5's lower bound requires S,A≥10, D≥20 log_A S, and T≥DSA. Theorem 6 assumes at most a fixed number of MDP changes and uniformly bounded diameter. The proof includes concentration/episode analysis and an explicit extended-value-iteration convergence argument; the class excludes uncommunicating/transient-state MDPs unless modified.
